correctness.rationale: The two nonzero entries in the first Gaussian test column determine the unpivoted QR angle almost surely. Direct multiplication gives \(w_1^2=1-(1-\epsilon^2)s\) and \(w_2^2=\epsilon^2+(1-\epsilon^2)s\). For tau between epsilon and sqrt((1+epsilon^2)/2), rank 2 is retained exactly when \(u\le s\le 1-u\). Because Y/X is standard Cauchy, its two-sided interval gives (1). The rank-one optimal residual is epsilon by Eckart–Young–Mirsky. For the full algorithm, a failed initial lookahead implies \(X_1^2+X_2^2\le 2c^2\epsilon^2\), bounding its probability by the 2-degree chi-square CDF. The second lookahead is exactly zero on successful full-rank first QR, giving the joint-event bound (2). In the c-fixed scaling, Cauchy cutoffs tend to \(\sqrt{c^2-1}\) and infinity, yielding (3). Exact rational and simulated reproduction supplements this complete proof; no infinite claim is inferred from finite experiments.

value.rationale: Near-minimal rank for block-efficient matrix-free Frobenius QB is an explicit objective of [1], and the source pruning criterion is basis-row rather than rotation invariant. Formula (1) gives an exact quantitative failure rate for that motivated policy, with the full algorithm retaining twice the optimal rank on roughly half of well-separated near-rank-one inputs at \(\tau=\sqrt2\,\epsilon\); as c decreases to 1 the rate approaches one. The event persists despite exact zero residual before pruning and is not an estimator-noise artifact. This is a meaningful, natural algorithmic boundary beyond a textbook SVD fact; rotating to singular directions is credited as a conventional fix. It does not claim large-dimensional rate, runtime improvement, or a universal algorithmic failure.
